key_insight: GeoState separates true scene geometry changes from camera/view effects, making 3D world state prediction easier and more stable. Instead of treating geometry features as directly predictive, it learns a view-decoupled representation of world evolution.
problem_solved: Many 3D world models rely on geometry foundation model features that change with the camera view, which mixes actual scene dynamics with observation-dependent variation. This makes future state prediction harder and less reliable.
method: Learn a geometry state representation that is explicitly decoupled from viewpoint changes.
Model scene-state evolution separately from camera-dependent observations.
Use geometry foundation model features as input while removing view-induced entanglement for predictive world modeling.
impact: This can improve the stability and accuracy of predictive 3D world models by giving them a cleaner notion of scene state. For practitioners, it means better long-horizon reasoning, more robust geometry prediction, and more reliable world modeling from changing viewpoints.

paper_title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
paper_authors: Hongchang Liu, Jian Liu, Yujuan Ding, Liang Peng, Xun Jiang
